chunks: By this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
When water reaches the measure of a kurr, nothing renders it impure.

key_terms.كُرٌّ: kurr — a unit of water volume in Shia fiqh (approx. 377–384 liters); water at or above this threshold is immune from ritual impurity
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it ritually impure (Form II verb from najasa); negated here to establish legal immunity

ai.seo_question: According to Shia hadith, when does water become immune from ritual impurity (najasah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, establishes a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh: water that reaches the volume of one kurr cannot be rendered ritually impure by anything. The kurr is a precise volumetric measure (~377–384 liters) central to the Shia law of taharah, distinguishing large quantities of water (which resist najasah) from small quantities (which do not).
